title: The Jung Hotel band with Johnny Wiggs: stock orchestrations
summary: Hirsch gives a frank opinion of the Jung Hotel band, Wiggs as a player and the personnel (Stratikas, Wolf, Fridge, Roniga, Laocana).

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Johnny Harmon was at the John Hotel when I was there. He was in the band. You been a player? I wouldn't say so. He was, I don't know. Johnny was more of an authority than I think he was a player. I really don't, I really, I was never impressed by his playing. And that's not nice for me to say. Because he's built up quite a reputation as a teacher. Maybe I'm wrong. I don't know. We had him and Charlie Wagner. Both of them, both of them characters, believe me. I mean, their, habits were entirely different than a legitimate musician. Uh-huh. But, I mean, even Johnny Hyman, I mean, even, never even, you would never even use the name Johnny Hyman. Everything was Johnny Wiggs. You don't want to be known as Johnny Hyman.

But, I worked, he worked at the, the, the band at the, the band at the John Hotel, was, in my opinion, I mean, after, after you come to a realization of who you've worked with, you know, you've worked with. Who you've worked with and what they have, what you have accomplished and what you have done with whom you've worked with. It was, it was a rotten band. You can't, you can't get away from it. But it was, it was, it was a, it was a band that, that people liked.

Yeah, Stratikas, he was, he was a, not a, he was a good trombone player, but nothing, I mean, they were playing stock orchestration. This is no originality. And, we had Joe Schultz, Joe, Joe Wolf playing piano. And they used to call him Foxy Grandpa. He used to play like this. No rhythm at all, whatsoever. And we had a trump, a bass player by the name of Dave Fridge, who played the third trumpet on the, third trumpet on the tuba.
He wasn't playing boop, boop, boop. He was playing boop, boop, boop, boop.
And he was playing all of that. And then, Al Hestimer was playing guitar, which, to this day, he's not a guitar player.
Did they have any head arrangements or anything to make a difference? No. The Owls at least had that.

Strictly, there was strictly orchestrations. Seventy-five cents orchestrations, that was the book. Winstein was in that band with you? No. Johnny Roniga, Joe, Joe had a very good first album. The saxophone section was the best section of the band. Johnny Roniga on alto, and Joe Laocana, Erasmus Laocana was on first alto. He was a good, legitimate first alto player.
He sounded good with the Halfway House on the recordings. Yeah. I just heard some this morning.
Yeah. He was, Joe, Joe was a good.
